analects.title: Analects · Lúnyǔ 論語
analects.description: The sayings and conversations of Confucius as compiled by his school — the foundation text of the Confucian tradition. The archive holds James Legge's 1893 translation and Leonard A. Lyall's 1909 rendering.

great-learning.title: Great Learning · Dàxué 大學
great-learning.description: The short chapter on self-cultivation and ordered society, lifted from the Book of Rites into the Four Books by Zhu Xi. The archive holds James Legge's 1893 translation.

doctrine-of-the-mean.title: Doctrine of the Mean · Zhōngyōng 中庸
doctrine-of-the-mean.description: The Zhōngyōng — equilibrium and sincerity as the way of the noble person; the most metaphysical of the Four Books. The archive holds James Legge's 1893 translation.

zhuangzi.title: Zhuāngzǐ 莊子
zhuangzi.description: The second great Daoist classic — parable, paradox, and the free-and-easy wandering of the perfected person, in thirty-three chapters. The archive holds Herbert A. Giles's 1889 translation.

mencius.title: Mencius · Mèngzǐ 孟子
mencius.description: The dialogues and arguments of Mencius (Mèngzǐ), the second sage of the Confucian school — the fourth of the Four Books. The archive holds James Legge's 1861 translation.

classic-of-poetry.title: Classic of Poetry · Shījīng 詩經
classic-of-poetry.description: The oldest anthology of Chinese poetry — 305 odes, hymns, and songs gathered in the early Zhou. The archive holds three renderings: James Legge's 1876 metrical version, William Jennings's 1891 translation, and Legge's prose selection from Sacred Books of the East vol. III.

classic-of-filial-piety.title: Classic of Filial Piety · Xiàojīng 孝經
classic-of-filial-piety.description: A short dialogue on filial devotion as the root of all virtue, long a primer of Confucian moral teaching. The archive holds Ivan Chen's 1908 translation.

dao-de-jing.title: Dào Dé Jīng 道德經 (Laozi)
dao-de-jing.description: The founding classic of Daoism — eighty-one brief chapters on the Way and its power, attributed to Laozi. The archive holds four renderings: James Legge (1891), C. Spurgeon Medhurst (1905), Dwight Goddard and Henri Borel (1919), and Lionel Giles's 1904 selections.
